file_stem: RWB E1 038 Delegation of authority table as reference data
title: Delegation of authority table as reference data
goal: Approval limits by decision, product and amount as a versioned table the router queries by date
why: Who may approve a write-off or restructure is a bank regulation (DoA). Holding it as data keeps the router honest and every decision keeps its version.
ace_note: No ACE read. Amounts come from the decision being routed (Epic 2); the table itself is Workbench reference data.

writes.note: levels L1-L6 by decision, regulation item, product

reads.note: rows valid on the decision date

stores: Incident to RW-RISK when no row covers a decision (NOT_COVERED)

path.text: No duplicates, limits do not fall

rules: BR3: the lowest covering level on the decision date wins
BR5: a related-party write-off always goes to L1 (Board)
BR7: a decision keeps the version it was routed with (R-UNI-38)
BR8: Risk approves, never the loader
risks: Duplicate rows or falling limits -> refused (MSG-P1-002)
No covering row (e.g. HP before chapter 8) -> NOT_COVERED + incident (MSG-P7-010)
Decision log fails -> version not approved (MSG-P7-003)
example: DOA-2026.11 (95 limits, regulations 540031 / 690070) -> 218 rows: 109 MORTGAGE, 109 SSME
